clue.text: Pet cat in error given chicken feed…

indicators.note: something done in error is done wrongly, so these letters are set down in a wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has mistakenly fed the family cat the hens' grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link to 'error', but it is part of the fodder: PET CAT IN, rearranged as signalled by 'in error'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken feed is slang for a trivially small sum of money, a paltry payment.

clue.text: Early public relations exercise holding the doctor up

indicators.note: the first and last pieces hold the reversed doctor between them

parts.note: PT is physical training, exercise

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: An early-morning publicity workout keeps the doctor waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the doctor because this is a down clue; 'holding' places the result between the two abbreviations. 'Early' is the definition in its sense of on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt means punctual or on time, without delay, so arriving in good time.

clue.text: Man races around to break up old kitchen equipment

indicators.note: the races go round the word for break up

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, are the famous motorbike races on the Isle of Man
rive is an old verb meaning to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: Motorbike racing on the island is wrecking an antique kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland famous for its Tourist Trophy motorbike races; 'around' wraps those races round the old verb for split.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged iron stand once set over a fire to hold a pot or kettle.

clue.text: Making a couple of points like a Trojan hero

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
NE, north-east, is another compass point
as means like, in the manner of

explanation.surface: Someone is arguing a couple of points the way a Trojan hero would.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan prince of Virgil's epic who fled the burning city and founded Rome's line.

clue.text: Little beasts may well come from clean homes

indicators.note: the answer is said to be produced out of these letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: Small animals tend to come from tidy households.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small colour-changing lizards, so they are examples of small creatures.

clue.text: … eats, but makes disdain clear

definitions.meaning: to eat greedily and fast, wolfing food down
to jeer or mock openly at something

explanation.surface: Someone wolfs their food while sneering at it.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both gobbling food hungrily and scornfully mocking, two unrelated senses of the same word.

clue.text: Deceive 27-and it's 14!

definitions.note: points to 14 across, here in its verb sense of ponder

parts.note: to con is to trick or deceive
the answer to 27 across means a supporter, one who sides with something

explanation.surface: Tricking a follower, it turns out, is done on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Both cross-references matter: 27 is the supporter, giving SIDER, and 14 is the verb sense of the answer there, to think hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh something up carefully is to think it over at length.

clue.text: Wild about bad lad getting trifle

indicators.note: the word for wild goes about the jumbled lad

parts.note: feral means wild, untamed

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoilt, put out of order

explanation.surface: A badly behaved lad goes wild over a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' scrambles the lad and 'about' sets the wild word round it. 'trifle' is not the British custard dessert but a trivial thing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a piece of nonsense or showy trinket, something of no importance.

clue.text: Sweets on rising put weight on!

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: sweets in British English means puddings, desserts

explanation.surface: Eating puddings makes people gain weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put weight on' looks like getting fat, but it means emphasising a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay emphasis on a syllable or point is to give it extra force.

clue.text: Learn to change about one say in Japan

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round, or about, the letter for one
to change the letters of these words is to rearrange them into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A visitor sets out to learn how to adapt to life in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' belongs to the fodder: LEARNTO is rearranged by 'change' and placed 'about' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is one example of an Eastern country, so things there are, for instance, Far Eastern.

clue.text: Branch out, naturally

parts.note: read as a branch that grows outwards from a head by nature: the bony branching growth on a deer, not a tree's limb or a business expanding

explanation.surface: Advice to expand into new ventures in an easy, organic way.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag's bony headgear forks into tines like the branches of a tree, growing out naturally each year.

clue.text: Quietly serving men shaved and got ready

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers serving in the British Army
pared means trimmed or shaved thin

explanation.surface: Servants quietly shaved their master, getting him ready for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army, so men who serve in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare is to make ready, so having got ready is the past tense of that verb.

clue.text: Various individuals going under

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned word for sundry or several
people who plunge beneath the water's surface

explanation.surface: Assorted people disappearing beneath the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an archaic adjective meaning sundry and the plural of someone who swims underwater.

clue.text: Out of place, as the underworld found

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and a name for that realm
located means found

explanation.surface: Something is discovered out of place in the world of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A bone pushed out of its joint has been moved out of its proper position.

clue.text: Meant to be thoughtful

explanation.surface: Someone was intended to be considerate.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means intentional; as a verb it means to ponder at length before deciding.

clue.text: A writer and entertainer receiving a sovereign

indicators.note: the entertainer takes in, or receives, the other letters

parts.note: a singer is one kind of entertainer
a sovereign is a gold pound coin, and L is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: An author and a performer are given a gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is an old British gold coin worth one pound, abbreviated L (from Latin libra).
explanation.definitionFit: J. D. Salinger was an American novelist, author of The Catcher in the Rye.

clue.text: Close with a cheap sort of housing

parts.note: to bung is to close up or plug a hole
low prices are cheap ones

explanation.surface: A deal is closed on some cut-price homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-storey house is a common style of dwelling.

clue.text: There's evidence in some creatures to show an original mind

indicators.note: the word for evidence sits inside the word for creatures

parts.note: deer are a group of animals, some creatures
a sign is evidence or a trace of something

explanation.surface: Animals show proof of an intelligence behind their creation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at the argument from design for a creator; the answer is someone who creates, such as a fashion designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who devises new things, like clothes or products, is a creative thinker.

clue.text: A shrewd old tribesman-by no means obtuse

parts.note: cute can mean clever or shrewd, as in a cute move
the Angles were a Germanic tribe who settled in early England

explanation.surface: A clever ancient Angle was certainly no fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtuse' looks like a word for dim, matching 'shrewd', but it is the geometry sense: an angle of more than 90 degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry an angle below ninety degrees is the opposite of one wider than a right angle.

clue.text: It manifests itself in the staff being deferential

indicators.note: the word it turns up inside the word for staff

parts.note: a pole is a staff or long rod
taken as written

explanation.surface: Courtesy shows itself in how respectful the employees are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the staff' looks like employees, but it is a stick, and 'manifests itself in' places the clue's opening word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being courteous and respectful towards others is good-mannered behaviour.

clue.text: Write in on new diet

indicators.note: new says the letters are to be made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone writes in about a new diet.
explanation.definitionFit: To indite is an old word for composing or putting into words.

clue.text: A title correctly given

parts.note: a title is a right or legal claim, as in title to land

explanation.surface: A heading is given in the right way.
explanation.definitionFit: Aright is an old-fashioned adverb meaning properly or without error.

clue.text: A woman who's popular with the network

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a grid is a network of lines, such as the electricity grid

explanation.surface: A lady who is well liked by the broadcasting network.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, so any bearer of it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: He croons, possibly for a glass of sherry

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be some other arrangement, so rearrange them

explanation.surface: A singer warbles for a drink of sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall drinking glass for sherry or beer bears this name, also used for a sailing ship.

clue.text: State reflective British and Spanish articles will give lead

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so these articles are read backwards

parts.note: an is an English indefinite article
el is the Spanish definite article, the

explanation.surface: Official British and Spanish reports will take a lead on the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective' turns the two articles round as a pair, giving the end of the answer after Georgia. 'lead' is the metal, not taking charge.
explanation.definitionFit: This mineral is lead sulphide, the chief ore from which the metal is extracted.

clue.text: Deciding to quit work can be really impressive

definitions.meaning: walking out on a job as a protest

explanation.surface: Walking out of a job can make a strong impression.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both staging an industrial walkout and being eye-catching.

clue.text: Pay leftist to contain strife

indicators.note: the word for leftist holds, or contains, the word for strife

parts.note: a red is a communist or left-winger
war is strife or conflict

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist is paid to keep a dispute under control.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a payment or recompense given for some service.

clue.text: The supporter heard ten different versions

indicators.note: these letters are to be made into a different version of themselves, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A fan listened to ten alternative versions of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or backer of a cause or a leader is one who sticks to it.
